issues.description: The problem statement gives conflicting instructions about the SealSaloon.stock attribute: one part (lines 70-71) instructs students to initialize the stock in the SealSaloon constructor (implying an instance field initialized in the constructor), while a later note (lines 77-81) explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static and shared across all instances. These two requirements conflict (a static final shared stock cannot be meaningfully described as being initialized in the instance constructor), which can confuse students about whether stock should be an instance or a static field and where it should be initialized.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification so it is consistent: either (A) require a static final Stock shared across all SealSaloon instances and state that it should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer (not in the instance constructor), or (B) require a non-static final Stock initialized in the instance constructor. Update the problem statement to remove the contradictory instruction about initialization in the constructor if option (A) is intended. This matches the solution, which uses a static final Stock initialized at declaration.
